item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-09

Issues: 500 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-11-08 23:13 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-09

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw remains highly active, with 500 issues and 500 PRs touched in the last 24 hours. However, the ratio skews toward backlog churn rather than forward momentum: 333 PRs are open versus 167 merged/closed, and 378 issues are open/active versus 122 closed. A significant share of closed items today are tagged stale, indicating cleanup rather than resolution. One patch release (v2026.11.2) shipped, focused narrowly on privacy/trust-boundary hardening rather than functional fixes. Overall health reads as stable but strained: core stability issues around SQLite contention, gateway event-loop stalls, and memory growth are recurring, long-lived, and still open.

2. Releases

v2026.11.2 — Security/privacy patch, no breaking changes announced.

  • Keeps configuration secrets, conversation content, tool errors, and channel payloads out of diagnostic logs.
  • Enforces selected provider and navigation trust boundaries.
  • Releases MCP grants after warm CLI turns.
  • References: #191318, #174998
  • Migration notes: None stated. Operators relying on diagnostic logs for debugging secret-adjacent flows should expect redaction.
  • Caveat: v2026.11.2 does not address the open P0 updater issue (#193962), where the fix for the SQLite header-probe timeout can't be reached from 2026.10.10 via openclaw update.

3. Project Progress

167 PRs were merged/closed today (full list not provided; sampled PRs are overwhelmingly open). Notable in-flight work visible in the open PR set:

  • Control UI permissions inspection — read-only People/Roles views (#195408), a meaningful step toward multi-user/admin capability.
  • Android reliability cluster — pending-input display and receipt-based send recovery (#191610), pre-ack steer ownership (#195402), file-allowlist messaging (#191316), and accessibility fixes (#195194).
  • Memory efficiency — dropping duplicate embedding cache copies (#195369) and reducing live skill-catalog memory (#195418), both directly targeting the memory-growth issues below.
  • Sandbox/network — preventing multi-GB history downloads in shallow sandbox checkouts (#195433).
  • CLI/UX polish — several small fixes improving error messages for unknown providers/worktrees (#195430, #195447) and profile-aware workspace paths (#195448).

Several PRs were closed by the repository's "active-PR limit" and resubmitted (#195077, #195178, #195073), suggesting contributor throughput is outpacing review capacity.

4. Community Hot Topics

Item Comments Signal
#166634 — checkpoint failure after crash leaves agent permanently UNAVAILABLE 26 Highest-engagement issue; agent becomes unrecoverable
#191944 — macOS gateway stop fails with process-inspection error 25 Basic lifecycle command broken on Intel macOS
#38327 — "Cannot convert undefined or null to object" with google-vertex 18 (👍3) Long-lived P1 regression since 2026.3.2
#53408 — tool params silently dropped after long conversations 17 (👍2) Closed as stale despite serious data-integrity implication
#67413 — per-agent dreaming config 16 (👍5) Highest 👍 count; OOM from parallel dreaming

Underlying needs: Users are hitting recovery and resource-isolation problems — agents that won't come back after a crash, restarts/stops that misreport, and memory/tooling behavior that degrades over long sessions. The stale-closure of #53408 (silent parameter loss) is a notable community-friction risk: high-impact bugs are aging out without fixes.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity (as labeled):

P0 / Release blockers

  • #193962 — updater probe timeout blocks reaching the fix from 2026.10.10. Fix exists upstream (#187197, in 2026.11.5-beta.1) but is unreachable via openclaw update.
  • #162211 — startup blocks event loop 40–200s; health monitor misreads stall as disconnect → restart loop. No fix PR.
  • #158592 — post-sleep/wake runtime publication timeout; all inbound messages fail until restart. No fix PR.
  • #137177 — built-in WeCom plugin uninstallable.

P1 / Crash loops & data integrity

  • #181432 — baseline RSS ~1.9 GB (from ~300 MB) on ARM64; SQLite timeouts.
  • #185578 — heap floor ratchets ~25 MiB/h until V8 abort.
  • #182369 — off-heap RSS growth ~0.1 GiB/h, monitor never fires.
  • #191847 — SQLite worker OOM-killed at 512 MB; session permanently "admission is closed."
  • #117262 — 3 concurrent SQLite write handles → ~33s event-loop stalls.
  • #157255 — turn claim not released after lane timeout; 90+ min session wedge.
  • #163566 — session-resource-loader burns ~100s CPU per turn post-repair.
  • #126906 — denying write tool silently disables memory persistence and reports success (data-loss + silent failure).

Fix PRs exist (open): #195446 (prepared-runtime staleness), #195452/#195451 (doctor exit-non-zero blocking Telegram/rescue), #195369 (memory cache duplication), #195418 (skill catalog memory), #195178 (withdrawn plugin requests). No fix PRs are linked for the P0 crash-loop cluster.

Pattern: SQLite concurrency, memory growth (both heap and off-heap), and post-update/repair degradation form the dominant stability theme.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • Per-agent dreaming configuration (#67413) — highest 👍 (5); memory-spike/OOM driven. Closed stale, but likely to resurface.
  • SecretRef support in MCP env/headers (#76493, 👍6) — secret-management best practices blocked by schema.
  • Opt-in personal identity on iOS/macOS (#162164) — multi-user identity roadmap signal, already partially merged (#164593).
  • Tool schema token overhead reduction (#14785, ~3,500 tok/session) — cost-efficiency request.
  • Markdown preview in Review (#128090, 👍4); Android notification QoL (#143387); onboarding memory/embedding step (#16670).
  • Provider-aware backpressure for subagents (#126727); backup manifest omissions (#107433).

Prediction: The already-in-flight Control UI permissions work (#195408) and the memory-efficiency PR cluster (#195369, #195418) are the most likely to land next, given active PRs. SecretRef (#76493) and per-agent dreaming (#67413) are strong candidates for a near-term minor release if maintainers prioritize security/ops ergonomics.

7. User Feedback Summary

  • Reliability under recovery: Users report agents that never return after crashes (#166634), sleeps (#158592), or lane timeouts (#157255) — with no self-healing path.
  • Silent failures: Tool params dropped (#53408), memory saves falsely reported successful (#126906), and generic "CLI command failed" messages (multiple PRs today) erode trust.
  • Resource exhaustion: Memory growth on long-running gateways is a recurring operational pain (three separate P1 memory issues).
  • Platform gaps: macOS Intel service management (#191944) and Windows Docker bind-mount startup (#193262) break basic operations.
  • Positive signal: Sustained contributor volume (500 PRs/day touched), rapid Android/web-UI polish, and resubmission behavior indicate an engaged community despite review bottlenecks.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-unanswered high-value items needing maintainer attention:

  • #38327 — P1 regression open since March 2026 (8+ months), diamond-lobster rated, with a linked open PR. Longest-standing high-severity item.
  • #14785 — token overhead, open since Feb 2026, needs product decision.
  • #107433 — backup manifest omissions, open since July, tagged needs-security-review and needs-live-repro.
  • #76493 — SecretRef in MCP schema, open since May, needs security review.
  • #137613 — pre-compaction memory flush disabled on CLI backends, open since Sept.
  • #161158 — gateway restart misreports failure while exiting 0; hardcoded 60s budget.
  • Process concern: the clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr tag appears on the vast majority of top issues, and several serious bugs were closed stale (#53408, #67413). The maintainer-review queue appears to be the primary constraint on project throughput.

Data source: github.com/openclaw/openclaw, snapshot 2026-11-09. Totals reflect items updated in the prior 24h; PR comment counts were not present in the source data.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — Personal AI Assistant / Agent Open-Source Ecosystem

Snapshot date: 2026-11-09 · Projects: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw

1. Ecosystem Overview

The personal AI assistant/agent open-source landscape in November 2026 is characterized by a large, engaged contributor base but a systemic review-capacity bottleneck: across the five projects, ~140 PRs and ~70 issues were touched in 24 hours, yet only one project (ZeroClaw) merged a meaningful PR set and only one (OpenClaw) shipped a release. Projects are converging on a common architecture — gateway/daemon core, pluggable channel adapters (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WeCom/QQ), MCP tool integration, persistent memory, and sandboxed multi-agent orchestration — while differentiating mainly in identity/access models, memory implementation, and platform coverage. The dominant community-reported risk themes are silent failures (config resets, dropped tool params, undetected fallbacks), resource growth (SQLite contention, heap/off-heap RSS ratcheting), and multi-tenant isolation (shared memory leaking across users in group channels). Security hardening — secret redaction in logs, trust-boundary enforcement, A2A auth — is the fastest-moving change category across the board.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Issues (24h, open/total) PRs (24h, open/merged-closed) Releases (24h) Health Score* Notes
OpenClaw 378 open / 500 touched; 122 closed 333 open / 167 merged-closed v2026.11.2 (privacy patch) 6.5 / 10 Highest raw volume; stable but strained. P0 updater unreachable; large stale-closure of serious bugs; review queue is primary constraint.
Hermes Agent Majority open, 5 closed 50 open / 0 merged None 5.5 / 10 High engagement, zero integration velocity. 7-month-old security fix PRs unmerged. Two security issues triaged/closed.
IronClaw 0 updated 5 open (Dependabot) / 1 closed (superseded) None 4.5 / 10 Operationally quiet; pure dependency churn. Longest open PR 78 days (wasm runtime upgrade).
QwenPaw 7 active / all open 15 open / 0 merged None 5.5 / 10 Strong same-day issue→PR loop (txohyeah cluster) but no merges. Duplicate-fix PR pair (#8622/#8624).
ZeroClaw 14 updated / ~7 closed 43 open / 7 merged-closed None (v0.9.0 gated) 7.5 / 10 Highest effective velocity; organized milestone (#7432), stacked PRs, prompt bug fixes. Two new S2 auth/data bugs unfixed.

Health score is a synthesized 1–10 judgment weighting: merged-PR throughput, severity of open bugs, release cadence, contributor responsiveness, and backlog staleness. It is not a maintainer-published metric.

Aggregate: 4 of 5 projects had zero or near-zero merge throughput in the window — the single most consistent ecosystem-wide signal.

3. OpenClaw's Position

Advantages vs peers

  • Scale and maturity: 500 issues + 500 PRs touched/day is an order of magnitude above every peer (next largest: Hermes at 50/50; ZeroClaw at 14/50). Only project shipping a release in-window.
  • Breadth of surface: enterprise channels (WeCom), Android/web/desktop clients, CLI updater, multi-user Control UI — a superset of peer feature scope.
  • Android + web-UI polish velocity is unmatched (pending-input recovery, pre-ack steering, accessibility fixes all in open PRs today).

Technical approach differences

  • Ships as a Node/TS runtime with SQLite-backed state — peer projects are Rust (IronClaw/ZeroClaw) or Python (Hermes/QwenPaw). This correlates directly with its signature failure mode: SQLite write-handle contention causing multi-second to ~33s event-loop stalls — a class of bug largely absent in the Rust projects and handled differently in Python.
  • Updater-integrated release pipeline (openclaw update) is unique but currently its Achilles' heel: P0 #193962 blocks reaching the fix from 2026.10.10.

Community-size comparison

  • OpenClaw's daily touch volume (~1,000 items) implies a contributor base roughly 10× Hermes, ~20× QwenPaw/ZeroClaw, and >100× IronClaw. However, this volume is not translating into merged output (167 closed vs 333 open, with many closures tagged stale) — growth is outpacing governance.

Caveat for decision-makers: OpenClaw is the reference implementation by adoption, but its reliability posture (P0 crash loops without fix PRs, high-impact bugs closed as stale — e.g., #53408 silent tool-param loss) means adopters should pin versions and avoid relying on openclaw update until #193962 clears.

4. Shared Technical Focus Areas

Requirement Projects Specific Needs
Multi-tenant / per-user memory isolation Hermes (#17254, #28226), OpenClaw (#162164 identity work), ZeroClaw (roster identities #11264–#11313) Per-user_id memory namespacing; scoped dashboard chat for non-admins; shared-channel preference bleed is the #1 latent demand in Hermes.
Silent-failure elimination / observability QwenPaw (#8475, #8103), OpenClaw (#126906, #53408), Hermes (#148961 A2A auth degrades silently) Warning logs on config mutation; explicit fallback-model signaling; no success-report on failed writes.
Resource growth & concurrency correctness OpenClaw (P1 heap #185578, off-heap #182369, SQLite #117262), Hermes (cron session leaks #145314/#145791), QwenPaw (SQLite error masking #8620) Bounded RSS; lease release on lane timeout; duplicate-query elimination; real-error propagation.
MCP ecosystem hardening OpenClaw (#76493 SecretRef in MCP schema), Hermes (#118572 MCP metadata sanitization), ZeroClaw (MCP image results #10501) Secret management in env/headers; unicode-tag sanitization; OpenAI-provider interop.
Identity & gateway trust boundaries OpenClaw (v2026.11.2 trust boundaries), ZeroClaw (dashboard sign-in, JWKS), Hermes (A2A auth #148961) Sign-in lifecycle, authorization on disabled agents, config-write refusal on relay-served dashboards.
Multi-agent orchestration safety ZeroClaw (delegation workspace #9872, peer-turn durability #9597), OpenClaw (per-agent dreaming OOM #67413), QwenPaw (/steer #8318) Workspace sandboxing, attributable peer messaging, hop limits, mid-execution steering.
Cross-platform parity Hermes (Windows ACP hang #135977), OpenClaw (macOS Intel #191944), ZeroClaw (CI matrix #7461), QwenPaw (Windows desktop #8627) Windows/macOS test matrices; launchd/service lifecycle; long-path handling.
Cost/token efficiency OpenClaw (#14785 ~3.5k tok/session), QwenPaw (cron thinking levels #8626, row-only recall #8625), Hermes (KV-cache window #5306) Schema token overhead reduction; per-job model selection; retrieval optimization.

5. Differentiation Analysis

Dimension OpenClaw Hermes Agent IronClaw QwenPaw ZeroClaw
Core stack Node/TS + SQLite Python Rust (wasm runtime) Python Rust
Primary focus Full-surface personal assistant (channels + clients + admin) Message-platform agent w/ memory OS ambitions NEAR-ecosystem agent runtime Pragmatic chat-ops + Desktop beta Security-hardened gateway & multi-agent identity
Target users Power users, teams, multi-channel operators Community/group-chat deployments, Telegram/Discord/Feishu Blockchain/AI infra developers Cost-conscious production pipelines Self-hosted, SSO/OIDC operators, multi-agent teams
Distinctive bet Breadth + updater as a platform Multi-tenant memory as headline feature Runtime currency (wasm, dependency hygiene) Fast contributor loop, Desktop UX Identity/access control as first-class product
Signature weakness SQLite/event-loop contention; stale-closure of high-severity bugs Review freeze (0 merges; 7-month security PRs) Near-zero feature velocity; bot-only activity Unmerged backlog despite strong PR supply XL stacked-PR dependency chains aging 5–6 wk
Release signal v2026.11.2 privacy patch Biweekly historically, paused None 2.2.2.post1 stable / 2.3.0-beta.2 v0.9.0 gated on tracker #7432

Architecture differentiation summary:

  • Rust (IronClaw, ZeroClaw) trades development velocity for runtime stability — notably absent from the memory-growth and event-loop-stall bug classes that dominate OpenClaw's P1 list. ZeroClaw converts this into a security-first posture.
  • Python (Hermes, QwenPaw) enables fast contributor turnaround (QwenPaw's same-day issue→PR pairs) but exhibits Windows/platform fragility and concurrency leak patterns (cron leaks, worker-thread middleware skips).
  • Node/TS (OpenClaw) delivers the widest client surface at the cost of SQLite/event-loop contention and the heaviest review burden.

6. Community Momentum & Maturity

Activity tiers:

  • Tier 1 — Ecosystem anchor: OpenClaw (~1,000 daily touches, shipping releases, but governance-strained).
  • Tier 2 — Active but integration-bound: ZeroClaw (best velocity-to-organization ratio; milestone-driven), Hermes Agent (high engagement, zero merges — the clearest stalled-integration case).
  • Tier 3 — Niche/early: QwenPaw (responsive contributors, Desktop beta, no merges in-window), IronClaw (maintenance-only this period).

Rapidly iterating: ZeroClaw (v0.9.0 identity/gateway stack, stacked-PR discipline), OpenClaw's Android/web-UI surface, QwenPaw's bug-fix loop.

Stabilizing / consolidating: IronClaw (dependency churn only), OpenClaw's core (recurring long-lived stability issues indicate architectural limits now in maintenance mode rather than rapid evolution).

Maturity read:

  • Process maturity: ZeroClaw > OpenClaw > Hermes ≈ QwenPaw > IronClaw (milestone trackers and dependency-annotated stacked PRs vs. stale-closure and active-PR-limit churn).
  • Codebase maturity (stability): ZeroClaw ≈ IronClaw (Rust) > QwenPaw > Hermes > OpenClaw (most feature-rich, most stability debt).
  • Contributor retention risk: Highest at Hermes (7-month-old security PRs) and QwenPaw (3-month-old first-contributor auth fix #7066); lowest at ZeroClaw (explicit follow-up culture).

7. Trend Signals — Value for AI Agent Developers

  1. Silent failure is the new top-tier bug class. Across QwenPaw (#8475, #8103), OpenClaw (#126906, #53408), and Hermes (#148961), users are reporting behavior changes without signals — config resets, model swaps, dropped params, auth downgrades. Actionable: design agents with explicit fallback metadata, config-mutation warnings, and fail-loud write paths; treat "reports success but didn't" as a P0-class defect. This is a trust-architecture requirement, not a UX nicety.

  2. Review capacity, not contributor supply, is the ecosystem ceiling. Four of five projects had zero/near-zero merges despite 100+ PRs in flight. Actionable: adopt auto-merge for patch-level dependency groups (IronClaw pattern), consolidate stacked-PR dependencies (ZeroClaw pain), and run focused security-merge sprints (Hermes has 4 of its 5 oldest PRs as security fixes). For adopters: judge projects by merged security-fix latency, not issue volume.

  3. Multi-tenant memory is the next platform battleground. Hermes (#17254 + Memory OS #28226), OpenClaw identity work, and ZeroClaw roster identities all point the same direction. Actionable: build memory with user_id/tenant_id namespacing from day one; retrofitting isolation into a shared USER.md model is a multi-month drag.

  4. SQLite is a scaling cliff for agent state. OpenClaw's P1 cluster (write-handle contention, worker OOM, ~33s stalls) and QwenPaw's error-masking bug both stem from SQLite under concurrent agent workloads. Actionable: for multi-agent/concurrent deployments, evaluate Rust-native or externalized state stores, or strictly serialize writes with bounded queues and real-error propagation.

  5. Security hardening is the fastest-shipping change category. OpenClaw's only in-window release was privacy/trust-boundary; Hermes closed two security issues and has a backlog of redaction fixes; ZeroClaw is shipping JWKS/authorization policy. Actionable: expect breaking config changes around trust boundaries (e.g., ZeroClaw #11406 ! macOS broad-root refusal) — pin configs and read release notes.

  6. Identity-aware, scoped agent operations are entering the release pipeline (ZeroClaw v0.9.0 scoped dashboard chat, JWKS validation, relay-served config-write refusal). Actionable: if deploying agents to shared dashboards or group channels, plan for OIDC/JWKS integration and per-scope authorization now; "disabled ≠ inert" must be enforced at the gateway layer (see #12289).

  7. Cost/latency engineering is becoming a production requirement (per-job thinking levels, row-only recall, token-schema reduction, KV-cache budgeting). Actionable: expose model-selection and retrieval-granularity controls; users are running pipelines, not demos.

  8. Platform parity is a competitive differentiator, not a checkbox. Windows is a second-class citizen across Hermes (ACP hang), QwenPaw (desktop/git long-path), and OpenClaw (macOS Intel lifecycle); only ZeroClaw actively tracks a CI matrix fix (#7461). Actionable: treat cross-OS CI as release-gating for desktop/gateway products.

Bottom line for decision-makers: OpenClaw is the reference platform by adoption but carries the heaviest reliability and governance debt — pin versions, avoid the in-app updater until #193962 clears, and independently verify "closed" serious bugs. ZeroClaw is the best-organized project for security/identity-sensitive deployments. Hermes is the strongest multi-tenant memory bet if review capacity recovers. QwenPaw offers fast community responsiveness for cost-sensitive Python deployments. IronClaw is operationally quiet and best evaluated as a stable Rust runtime component rather than a feature platform.

Peer Project Reports

Hermes Agent — nousresearch/hermes-agent

Hermes Agent — Project Digest

Date: 2026-11-09 · Source: github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent

1. Today's Overview

Hermes Agent shows very high community activity but near-zero merge throughput: 50 issues and 50 PRs were touched in the last 24h, yet 0 PRs were merged or closed and no releases were published. The issue mix skews toward bugs (majority of the top-commented items carry type/bug), with a long tail of P2/P3 regressions across cron, gateway, desktop, and platform adapters. Notably, five issues were closed today (including type/security items #80936 and #118572), indicating triage is active even if integration is not. The 50-item open PR backlog with no merges is the clearest health signal: review bandwidth is the current bottleneck, not contributor supply. Overall: healthy engagement, stalled integration velocity.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24h. (Recent versions referenced in issues include v0.20.0, v0.22.5, v0.22.7, and v0.23.0, suggesting a roughly biweekly cadence prior to this window.)

3. Project Progress

Merged/closed PRs today: 0. No features advanced to main via PR merge in this window.

Issues closed today (5):

  • #88579 — Slack clarify button labels truncate on mobile (fixed)
  • #151237 — Missing labels on recent issues (labeling pipeline restored)
  • #80936 — redact_sensitive_text misses cookie-shaped credentials (security hardening)
  • #118572 — MCP server metadata bypasses unicode-tag sanitization (security)
  • #80483 — Cron misparses named Telegram private-DM topics (fixed)

Assessment: Two security-boundary issues resolved is a positive signal, but closure without accompanying merged PRs (or at least none visible in this window) means the fixes may be landing via direct commits or were resolved as already-fixed/duplicate. This should be verified by maintainers.

4. Community Hot Topics

Ranked by comment count:

# Item Comments Signal
1 #80280 Kanban stale/superseded worker process groups 7 👍1 Concurrency correctness — stale + replacement workers mutate the same worktree. Serious data-integrity risk for agent orchestration.
2 #17254 Multi-user preference memory 7 Multi-tenant memory isolation — shared USER.md leaks preferences across users in Feishu/Discord/Telegram groups. High-demand, needs-decision tag.
3 #145314 Quiet cron leaves permanent empty session 7 Cron hygiene — session leak per firing.
4 #135977 hermes acp hangs on Windows 6 Platform-blocking — session/new never returns; Windows users blocked.
5 #148414 Webapp menu overflow at non-100% UI scale 4 Desktop UX — visible, reproducible.
6 #144754 launchd update-restart undischargeable 4 macOS update lifecycle — fails closed on supervised hosts.

Underlying needs analysis:

  • Two of the top three threads concern multi-user/multi-tenant isolation (#17254, plus the related Memory OS proposal #28226). This is the loudest latent demand: Hermes is being deployed in shared channels and the memory model assumes a single user.
  • Agent process lifecycle correctness (#80280) is the most technically consequential — concurrent process trees mutating shared worktrees is a silent corruption path, not just a nuisance.
  • Cron session leakage appears twice in the top tier (#145314, #145791), suggesting a systemic resource-leak theme rather than one-off bugs.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity (per reporter-assigned priority and blast radius):

P2 — High

  • #151280 Stale-stream watchdog kills live streams. Ignores SSE ping/comment keepalives; terminates a live chat_completions stream at 240s during long Claude Opus thinking behind OpenAI-compatible proxies. No fix PR linked.
  • #148961 🔒 A2A auth silently degrades to localhost-only / no auth on systemd installs (env scrubbing of *TOKEN*). Security-relevant misconfiguration that fails open in a subtle way.
  • #151246 🔒 Routed-profile middleware skipped on worker threads → privacy plugin fails open. Profile isolation broken on Desktop multiplex.
  • #151247 Routed-profile child env strips MNEMOSYNE_EMBEDDING_* → memories stored without vectors. Silent data-quality degradation.
  • #151351 Desktop Windows ticket bridge kills python helper on timers → full boot re-run from one slow ticket.
  • #145314 / #145791 Cron empty-session leaks (two variants).
  • #151385 Removing/pausing cron job orphans non-terminal incidents — ledger unreconcilable.
  • #144728 session.resume omits running/status for live unpersisted sessions → composer locks.
  • #135977 Windows ACP hang (platform-blocking).
  • #82255 Env strip removes CONDA_PREFIX but leaves CONDA_SHLVL → breaks conda.

P3 — Moderate

  • #149026 Cookie-auth writes 403 behind TLS-terminating router (Origin stripped).
  • #149621 Empty ~/.bash_profile shadows ~/.profile → hermes missing from PATH.
  • #143001 Telegram document albums rejected (media_text_inlined_length).
  • #151053 Completion notification becomes empty for long single-line output.
  • #148414 Webapp menu overflow at non-100% UI scale.

Fix PRs visible: The top 20 PRs are predominantly older (April–August 2026) bug/security fixes still awaiting merge. None of today's P2 bugs appear to have a linked fix PR yet — a concerning gap given several are security-boundary issues.

Note on spam: Two issues opened today (#151517, #151518) are empty "probe" issues from kyanite-factory-bot[bot]. Recommend rate-limiting/reporting.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Most requested:

  1. Multi-user preference memory (#17254) — per-user_id memory isolation with independent storage. Paired with the broader Memory OS acceptance layer proposal (#28226) covering diagnostics, inventory, and isolation tests. Prediction: multi-tenant memory isolation is the single most likely headline feature for the next minor release given duplicate demand and needs-decision labeling.
  2. UI localization / i18n (#114195) — display.language in config.yaml, pt-BR requested first. Low-effort, high-reach; plausible near-term.

PR-side feature candidates awaiting merge:

  • Per-topic skill binding + auto-discovery for Telegram forums (#5489)
  • Dual message queue: follow-up (Alt+Enter) + steering (#5319)
  • Sliding-window context budget for KV-cache prefix optimization (#5306)
  • Raise default memory char limits (#5323)
  • One-shot handoff for next-session tasks (#5310)

Ecosystem signal: Multiple plugin-catalog PRs landed today — seedguard (#151543), salts-secrets (#151411), proof-run (#151252), plus a three-plugin SHA bump (#149734). The plugin ecosystem is warming up, with a notable theme of secrets firewalls and identity/context isolation — corroborating the multi-tenant demand above.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points expressed:

  • Shared-agent deployments break the memory model. Users running Hermes in group chats report cross-user preference bleed — a fundamental fit issue for team/community use cases.
  • Windows is a second-class platform right now. ACP hang, desktop ticket-bridge instability, and process-tree issues are concentrated there.
  • Cron is leaky. Practitioners running scheduled/monitor jobs accumulate empty sessions and orphaned incidents — operational hygiene debt.
  • Security-conscious users are finding real gaps (cookie redaction, A2A auth degradation, profile middleware skip, MCP metadata injection). These are reported with care and process-level evidence, indicating sophisticated users, not noise.
  • Update lifecycle friction on macOS launchd and Linux PATH — install/upgrade ergonomics need attention.

Satisfaction signal: Reports are detailed, reproducible, and often include proposed patches (e.g., #82255 discloses AI-assisted authorship with a patch attached). Community members are doing triage-grade work — a sign of investment, but also of review-capacity shortfall.

8. Backlog Watch

Oldest high-value PRs awaiting merge (all created ~2026-04-05/06, still open after ~7 months):

PR Age Why it matters
#5516 _detect_tool_failure structured-JSON handling ~7 mo Correctness of failure detection — blast-broad risk tag.
#5459 🔒 Redact signed vision image URLs ~7 mo Security; signed URLs leak in logs.
#5418 🔒 Harden Solana skill (SSRF/URL injection) ~7 mo Security; environment-controlled RPC_URL.
#5341 🔒 WeCom credential log redaction ~7 mo Security; access tokens in INFO logs.
#5300 🔒 Mattermost media URL redaction ~7 mo Security; bearer credentials in logs.

Also watch:

  • #80280 Kanban worker process-group race — top-commented issue, no fix PR, high corruption risk.
  • #17254 Multi-user memory — needs-decision; needs maintainer steering to avoid another 7-month wait.
  • #28226 Memory OS acceptance layer — design doc that could absorb #17254.

Recommendation: The backlog pattern — four of the five oldest open PRs are security fixes — is the most actionable finding. A focused security-merge sprint would both reduce risk and signal responsiveness to the community's highest-quality contributions, while unblocking the 50-PR queue that has gone merge-dry for 24h.

QwenPaw — agentscope-ai/QwenPaw

QwenPaw Project Digest — 2026-11-09

1. Today's Overview

QwenPaw shows high-velocity, maintenance-heavy activity with 7 active issues and 15 open PRs updated in the last 24 hours, but zero merges and zero releases — a pure intake day with no completions. Item Comments Link

  • Pain point #2 — Windows/Desktop beta instability. Issue #8627 shows environment-dependent failures (Git long paths, DAACL/temp-dir restrictions in #8568) that block Windows Hub Local users from installing default skills.

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-09

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw shows very high development velocity with 50 PRs and 14 issues updated in the last 24 hours, indicating an active, healthy open-source project. The activity is heavily concentrated around the v0.9.0 release milestone, specifically gateway/dashboard sign-in, scoped dashboard chat, and identity-access work. Notably, no new releases were published today. The open-PR backlog is large (43 open vs. 7 merged/closed), suggesting review capacity may be a bottleneck relative to contribution volume. 2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours. Omit.

No PRs were merged/closed with publicly reported summaries beyond the following closed items today:

  • #10501 → #10502 (Closed) — MCP tool-result images no longer return HTTP 400 on OpenAI-compatible providers by relocating image parts to a user message. Fix PR #10502 was closed alongside the issue. This closes a real interoperability bug affecting MCP workflows.

Item Signal Underlying Need

#7461 — CI matrix on Windows/macOS 5 comments, priority:p2 Cross-platform reliability — the test suite only runs on Linux while Lint/Build already run on three OSes.

Analysis: The dominant theme is multi-tenant, identity-aware agent operations (dashboard sign-in, scoped chat, roster passwords, relay-served dashboards). The second theme is multi-agent safety and attribution (delegation sandboxing, peer turn durability, relay-chain bounding). Maintainer attention is being pulled toward security hardening of the gateway/RPC boundary.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity:

  1. S2 — #12289: Disabled agents still run turns via operator WebSocket chat and restricted RPC. No fix PR linked yet. This is a security-relevant authorization gap (disabled ≠ inert) and should be prioritized.
  2. S2 — #9872: Bounded delegate writes to delegator's workspace instead of its own. priority:p1, risk:high. No fix PR yet; sandbox-isolation regression for multi-agent setups.
  3. S2 — #12288: "Discard all" retains drafts later persisted by a section Save — web dashboard data-integrity bug (a discarded value can be saved).
  4. P1 — #10501 (FIXED via #10502): MCP image tool-results caused HTTP 400 on OpenAI-compatible providers.
  5. #12096 — Dashboard sign-ins dropped during IdP outages/429/5xx (re-verification conflates unreachable with refused). Reliability/UX risk for self-hosted SSO.
  6. #11868 (PR) — Agent may repeat identical tool calls before dispatch; PR proposes pre-dispatch refusal plus closeout retention.

Takeaway: Two open S2 issues (#12289, #12288) touch authorization and data persistence, both introduced recently (dated 2026-11-08). The disabled-agent bug is the most urgent stability/security item of the day.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Request Link Likely v0.9.0?
Scoped dashboard chat for non-admin accounts #11984 Yes — tagged release:v0.9.0; implementation in #12244/#12298
Gateway tests: JWKS validation, failed writes, retirement race #11985 Likely alongside scoped chat
Non-admin agent creation with bounded risky fields #12290 Possible follow-on
Refuse credential/sign-in config writes on relay-served dashboards #12285 Security hardening, likely v0.9.x
Bash/zsh grammar-aware command policy #12296, PRs #11994, #12295 In progress
Peer-relay chain hop bounds (A→B→A) #12287 Follow-up to #9597, maybe v0.9.x
Durable, attributable peer-agent turns #9597 Larger effort; may miss v0.9.0

Prediction: v0.9.0 will be anchored by dashboard identity + scoped chat + gateway security policy publication, with shell-grammar policy improvements and platform CI matrix as stabilizing companions. Peer-agent durability and relay-chain bounds are more likely v0.9.x/v0.10.

7. User Feedback Summary

  • Pain points surfaced today: multi-agent delegation writing to the wrong workspace (#9872), dashboard form drafts not truly discarded (#12288), disabled agents still being reachable (#12289), and sign-ins dropping during identity-provider outages (#12096). These are safety, correctness, and reliability complaints from users operating agents in shared/dashboard contexts.
  • Use cases implied: multi-agent "delegator/executive-assistant → researcher" topologies; self-hosted dashboard with OIDC; MCP tool pipelines carrying images; Bash/zsh shell policy on macOS defaults.
  • Satisfaction signal: constructive, follow-up-oriented issue culture (maintainer-requested follow-ups like #12287 from #9597; stacked PR discipline with explicit dependency notes) suggests engaged, satisfied contributors even where bugs are found.
  • Dissatisfaction signal: review latency — many needs-author-action/do-not-merge XL PRs sit open since late September/October, which can frustrate authors (e.g., #11226, #11265, #11313).

8. Backlog Watch

Long-lived, high-importance items needing maintainer attention:

  1. #7432 — release-blocking v0.9.0 tracker (open since 2026-06-09). Its progress directly determines release timing.
  2. #7461 — Windows/macOS CI matrix (open since 2026-06-10, in-progress, 5 comments). Cross-platform regressions remain unguarded until this lands.
  3. #11322 / #11320 — plugin webhook RPC (open since 2026-10-01, size:XL, stacked, needs-author-action). The dependency chain (#11319→#11339→#11165→#11186→#11320→#11322) is a maintenance burden; a maintainer review/merge cadence would unblock a large feature cluster.
  4. #11265 / #11264 / #11313 — password lifecycle/authorization publication stack (open since Sept 30–Oct 1, risk:high, stacked). Identity-access is a strategic area; aging XL PRs here risk bit-rot.
  5. #11301 — agent rename committed-rename recovery across CLI/gateway/RPC (priority:p1, size:XL, open since 2026-10-01). Addresses state stranding on failed rename — high user impact if unresolved.

Health Assessment

Overall: Healthy and highly active, with review-capacity risk. Security and identity work is well-organized via trackers and stacked PRs, and bugs are being fixed promptly (#10501). However, the ratio of open (43) to closed (7) PRs, combined with multiple XL/needs-author-action PRs aging 5–6 weeks, suggests bottlenecked maintainer review. The two new S2 bugs (#12289, #12288) are recent and unfixed — they should be triaged ahead of the v0.9.0 gateway feature work to avoid shipping authorization gaps in the release.

item.content:encoded:
AI 基础设施日报 2026-11-09

生成时间: 2026-11-08 23:13 UTC | 覆盖项目: 6 个

  • vLLM
  • SGLang
  • llama.cpp
  • Ollama
  • LiteLLM
  • Unsloth

横向对比

跨项目对比报告 — 2026-11-09

1. 生态概览

今日的摘要显示，一个成熟的 AI 基础设施栈正在三个方向上同时收敛：Blackwell/SM120 消费级 GPU 支持在所有服务引擎上仍然不稳定（vLLM 和 SGLang 在 RTX PRO 6000 / GB10 硬件上都存在未解决的 decode/prefill 回归），量化 MoE 服务已成为主要的正确性风险面（SGLang 报告了两个静默垃圾输出的 router 加载 bug；vLLM 存在 SM120+NVFP4+MTP 非法内存访问回归），而 AMD/ROCm 正在获得大量投入（vLLM 的 persistent_topk 和 gfx942 FP8 MoE 配置、SGLang 的 gfx1250 UALink 和 AITER FlyDSL 路径）。与此同时，网关层正在承接更多生产职责——LiteLLM 的队列显示，计费核算和协议转换 bug 与路由吞吐同样重要。本地运行时（llama.cpp、Ollama）正从另一个方向收敛到相同主题：投机解码正确性、MoE 部分卸载，以及硬件多样性后端（RISC-V、Rockchip NPU、SYCL/Vulkan）。

2. 活跃度对比

项目 Issue（24 小时） PR（24 小时） 发布状态 值得关注的信号
vLLM 高（10 个已排序回归 + 活跃 RFC） 大量进行中（Kimi K3.1 TP8 系列、Marlin→Humming） 24 小时内无发布；v0.33.0 带有已知 SM120 回归 进行中最大的结构性优化提案（Humming kernel 迁移）
SGLang 高（隐含 56 张工单式积压；10 个已排序） 活跃（统一内存重构栈、Rust server 后续工作） 24 小时内无发布；v0.5.23 存在 GLM-5.3-Flash 损坏 最高严重级别的正确性 bug（静默 MoE router 故障）
llama.cpp 中等（10 个已排序） 密集合并日（b12202–b12211 已落地；新的 clip.h 移除） 约 10 个构建已落地（b12199–b12211） 所有项目中发布最多；确定性 Top-K 是可复现性的胜利
Ollama 中等（9 个已排序） 活跃（Rockchip NPU、FP8 导入、VRAM 预测） 24 小时内无发布 按模型的 num_parallel 终于实现（#9546）
LiteLLM 非常高（56 个 issue 更新） 非常高（304 个 PR 涉及） 开发标签 v1.110.0-dev.2（cosign 签名镜像） 变动最频繁；计费正确性 bug 占主导
Unsloth 中等（bug 报告） 非常高（同日大量 CLOSED 批次 + 开放后续工作） 24 小时内无发布 扩散/Studio 路径是活跃前沿

解读表格： LiteLLM 的 issue/PR 量比服务引擎高一个数量级——部分原因是网关面广，部分原因是承担计费语义的成本。llama.cpp 是唯一持续发布构建的项目，这与其作为底层参考运行时的角色一致。

3. 模型支持竞赛

模型 / 架构 vLLM SGLang llama.cpp Ollama Unsloth
Kimi K3.1（TP8） ✅ 3/5 拆分进行中 — — — —
MiniMax M3 / M3.1 ✅ Attention 复制标志 + NVFP4 索引分片 — — — —
Nemotron 3.5 ASR 流式 🟡 FR + 持久状态 PR — — — —
Qwen3.5/3.8（GDN 混合） 🟡 MTP drafter 修复 ✅ AITER causal conv1d prefill ✅ SSM d_state=64 快速路径 — ✅ Qwen-Image CFG 修复
DeepSeek-V4.1 — 🟡 SM120 上 8× prefill 回归 ✅ RPC 加载快 5×（开放） — —
Mixtral / Llama 4 / Qwen3-MoE（FP8 router） — 🔴 静默 router bug — — —
GLM-5.3-Flash / GLM-V — 🔴 v0.5.23 引擎损坏 — — —
FLUX.3 / HiDream / 图像生成 — ✅ HiDream-O1-Image（进行中） — ❌ macOS 不支持 ✅ fp8/fp16/Turing 路径
InternLM3 / TeleChat2/3 ✅ HF Transformers 后端迁移 — — — —
Rockchip RK3588/RK3576 — — — ✅ NPU prefill 后端 —

谁领先： vLLM 在新前沿模型支持的广度上领先（Kimi、MiniMax、Nemotron），并正在将长尾架构标准化到 HF Transformers 后端——这是一个减少逐模型维护成本战略赌注。SGLang 在AMD 特定模型路径（gfx950 上 Qwen GDN 的 AITER）和扩散方面领先。llama.cpp 拥有架构通用的胜利（SSM scan、MXFP4 RISC-V 重打包）。Ollama 是唯一推进到非 GPU 加速器（Rockchip NPU）的项目——一个独特的边缘部署赌注。

4. 性能前沿

优化工作集中在四个集群，分布不均：

KV cache——最热前沿。 vLLM 有最激进的议程：提议的 AMD 3-bit Octave KV cache（#59773），以及在 Triton/eager 后端缓存 K/V 视图派生。llama.cpp 正在 CUDA fattn-mma-f16 内融合 q8_0/q4_0 KV 反量化（#31802），并修复循环状态的 sticky-NaN（#31913）。SGLang 正在通过同批次前缀共享（#48963）攻击冗余 prefill KV。Ollama 的贡献是预测——准确的混合/量化 KV VRAM 预测（#19609）。

量化——正确性风险所在。 SGLang 的静默 MoE router bug（#49185、#49198）是今天最严重的 issue，正是因为量化 router 失败时不会报错。vLLM 的 Marlin→Humming 迁移（#65560）是进行中最大的结构性 kernel 变更，在 NVIDIA 各架构上整合 INT4/FP8/MXFP*/NVFP4 路径。Unsloth 的 INT8 融合 MLP 工作（#17114）和 Turing INT8 启用（#17167）将量化训练/推理扩展到更旧的硬件。

Kernel 与后端——AMD/Blackwell 是目标。 vLLM：ROCm persistent_topk（#63847）、gfx942 FP8 MoE（+12–25% 吞吐，#63727）。SGLang：FlyDSL causal conv1d、gfx1250 UALink all-reduce、FA3 kernel 选择调优（1.5–3% 差距）。llama.cpp：SYCL Battlemage decode 路径、用于投机验证的 OpenCL q8_0 GEMV。

分布式服务与调度。 vLLM 的 MiniMax attention 复制标志是一个务实的跨节点 TP 杠杆；SGLang 的统一内存/HiCache 重构（6 个 PR）和 Q4 P/D 分离路线图是最结构化的努力；Ollama 的调度器 VRAM 超额提交修复（#19581）是本地运行时的对应物。

值得注意的缺失： 批处理层面的创新今天很稀疏——大多数收益是 kernel 和内存布局层面的，而非调度器层面的（SGLang 的 max_running_requests/cuda_graph_max_bs 交互仍然是一个吸收态调优陷阱，#33483）。

5. 层级定位

层级 项目 主要价值 今日焦点
服务引擎（数据中心） vLLM、SGLang 吞吐、前沿模型首日支持、分布式服务 Kimi/MiniMax 支持、Blackwell 修复、AMD kernel、静默正确性 bug
本地/边缘运行时 llama.cpp、Ollama 可移植性、硬件多样性、单二进制/桌面 UX 确定性采样、SSM 卸载、Rockchip NPU、按模型并行
LLM 网关 LiteLLM 路由、预算、协议转换、可观测性 计费核算正确性、/v1/messages 保真度、热路径 Python 消除
训练 / 微调 Unsloth 内存高效训练、扩散 Studio、量化感知微调 扩散管线修复、INT8/Turing、线程安全并发加载

各层正在收敛到重叠的职责：vLLM 和 SGLang 现在都实现了类 OpenAI API 表面和类网关路由（P/D 分离、回退）；LiteLLM 正在将热路径迁移到 Rust 以支撑 1,000+ 部署；Ollama 正在吸收过去隐含的运行时关注点（VRAM 预测、调度器）。随着 litellm 将性能关键逻辑推入 Rust，服务引擎暴露更丰富的原生 API，网关层传统角色的压力将持续存在。

6. 趋势信号

1. 静默正确性故障是量化 MoE 的决定性风险。 SGLang 的 router bug（#49185、#49198）输出垃圾且无错误；vLLM 的 SM120/NVFP4/MTP 回归（#65139）和 llama.cpp 在量化目标上的投机解码分歧（#25618）属于同一类。给开发者的行动： 在任何量化 MoE 升级前，针对参考检查点构建 logit 一致性或黄金输出测试——活性检查不会捕获这些。

2. 预算执行不能仅信任网关层。 LiteLLM 的 #50124/#50125/#50528 三件套（缺失用量 → 未计费；超预算串行准入；断连留下预留）意味着 max_budget 是尽力而为。行动： 将网关预算与上游提供商配额和客户端总截止时间配对（x-litellm-timeout 限制每次尝试，而非墙钟时间，#49751）。

3. 投机解码是可复现性风险，而不仅仅是性能旋钮。 llama.cpp 前三大 issue 中有两个是投机解码正确性/中止（#30860/#31914、#25618）。行动： 如果你运行评估框架、agent 重放或回归套件，要么使用 bf16 目标，要么在量化模型上禁用 draft-MTP 并固定构建版本。

4. Blackwell 消费级 GPU（SM120）在各引擎上尚未生产就绪。 vLLM decode 崩溃（#56892）和 SGLang 的 8× DSV4.1 prefill 回归（#49173，源于过严的 is_sm(10) 门控）都指向不成熟的 SM120 路径。行动： RTX 50xx / RTX PRO 6000 / GB10 部署应针对 SM100 级参考数字进行验证并跟踪修复，不要假设功能对等。

5. AMD 正在成为一等服务目标——且带模型特定调优。 Octave 3-bit KV、gfx942 FP8 MoE 配置、gfx1250 UALink、AITER GDN kernel。行动： 如果 MI300X/MI355 或 RDNA 在你的路线图中，为引擎特定 kernel 启用预留预算；不要假设 CUDA 调优配置可以迁移。

6. 流式/agent 基础设施是下一个战场。 vLLM 的调度器拥有持久状态（#65544）解锁有状态 ASR/语音 agent；SGLang 的可缓存 agent 前缀 RFC（#47763）和同批次 KV 共享（#48963）针对 agent 循环 TTFT；llama.cpp 的 UTF-8 工具调用清理（b12199）和语法排序 PR 解决最常见的 agent 失败模式。行动： agent 框架构建者应跟踪这三条线索——它们直接影响 TTFT、工具调用可靠性和多轮成本。

7. 优雅运维仍然服务不足。 vLLM 的 --shutdown-timeout bug（#61562）意味着 DP>1 部署上的滚动重启会以 500 丢弃在途请求；Ollama 的 runner 卸载失败可能超额提交 VRAM（#19577）。行动： 对于生产滚动升级，明确验证排空行为，并预期在 vLLM 修复落地前出现 500。

8. 扩散/图像生成是微调栈中新兴的工作负载类别。 Unsloth 的同日 CLOSED 批次绝大多数是扩散（CFG 配对、NVFP4 解码、VAE 分块、设备定位），带有开放的 fp8-on-L4 和线程安全回归。行动： 如果 Studio 驱动的图像/视频管线在范围内，固定提交并在 #17171 落地前避免并发扩散模型加载。

各项目详细报告

vLLM — vllm-project/vllm

vLLM 摘要 — 2026-11-09

1. 今日要闻

过去 24 小时内没有新版本发布，但 issue/PR 队列显示围绕 Kimi K3.1 服务（KV cache/attention 拆分 PR）以及一组 SM120/Blackwell 消费级 GPU 问题（涉及 CUDA graph 捕获和 MTP 投机解码）的活动非常密集。在优化方面，正在进行中最大的结构性变更是提出的跨 NVIDIA 架构的 Marlin → Humming 内核迁移，同时还有针对 AMD GPU 的新 3-bit Octave KV cache RFC。

2. 版本发布与破坏性变更

过去 24 小时内没有新版本发布。值得注意的进行中变更及其兼容性影响：

  • RFC：移除 Group Activation Ordering（actorder=group） — 提议从 vLLM、compressed-tensors 和 llm-compressor 中移除运行时 actorder 支持，影响使用 actorder=group 量化的 GPTQ W4A16/W8A16 模型。已关闭/停滞，但对拥有此类 checkpoint 的用户具有迁移相关性。#48148
  • llguidance 在 vllm==0.33.0 中成为无条件依赖，并且被 from vllm import LLM 导入，这会在 glibc < 2.31 的环境上阻塞安装/导入。#66345

3. 新模型与硬件支持

  • Kimi K3.1 @ TP8 — K3.1 服务系列的第 3/5 部分拆分，添加了在张量并行 8 下服务 K3.1 所需的 KV cache 和 attention 变更（第 1/5 和 2/5 部分已合并）。#66037
  • Nemotron 3.5 ASR Streaming（0.6B） — 功能请求，支持 NVIDIA 的流式多语言 ASR 模型；配套 PR 为会话状态固定大小且不可重计算的流式模型添加调度器持有的持久状态。#47455、#65544、RFC #65545
  • MiniMax M3 — 实验性 VLLM_MINIMAX_M3_REPLICATE_ATTN=1 在 TP rank 间复制 attention（跳过 attention all-reduce，MoE 保持 TP），适用于跨节点 TP 较慢的场景；另一个 PR 将 MiniMax M3.1 的 NVFP4 index cache 与 indexer CP 分片。#66378、#64631
  • Transformers 后端迁移 — InternLM3、IQuestCoder、TeleChat2/2.5 和 TeleChat3 从 vLLM 的 Llama 实现迁移到 HF Transformers 建模后端（新增 TeleChat2-115B 支持）。#66416
  • ROCm：Mamba2 ReplaySSM + 投机解码 在 Triton 后端上（此前仅限 FlashInfer/CUDA），并附带 B200 nightly 评估的 MI355 镜像。#66318

4. 性能与优化

  • RFC：跨 NVIDIA 架构用 Humming 替换 Marlin — Humming 现已覆盖 Marlin 的格式（INT4/INT8 GPTQ/AWQ、FP8、MXFP8、MXFP4、NVFP4、MXFP6），适用于 dense 和 MoE 层；Marlin 属于 SM80 时代，没有 Hopper/Blackwell 专用路径。#65560
  • ROCm persistent_topk 采样移植（FilteredTopK + sampled_topk 层级，wave64 安全的 HIP 宏）；gfx950 的每个 batch 都走大 LDS 路径。#63847
  • gfx942 FP8 W8A8 fused-MoE 配置 针对 E=32、N=4096（Muse Spark 在 TP8+EP 下）：在 MI300X 上 64 并发请求时服务吞吐提升 12–25%，GSM8K 不变。#63727
  • RFC：Octave KV，AMD GPU 的原生 3-bit KV cache — 动机来自在 4× RX 7900 XTX 上服务长 prompt 的 Qwen3.8-27B W4A16。#59773、PR #59774
  • Triton/eager attention 后端在每次调用时重新推导 K/V cache 视图 — 与 #59534 中 FlashAttention 修复同类开销；提议缓存这些视图。#64572
  • 投机解码：零气泡 draft-token 交接，用于使用 step_with_batch_queue 时的结构化输出。#64531
  • RFC：ViT 完整 CUDA Graph — 跟踪捕获整个 ViT 前向（Qwen3-VL、GLM-V、Kimi K2.5）以减少多模态服务中的启动开销。#38175

5. 稳定性与回归

按严重程度排序：

  1. SM120 解码吞吐崩溃 / CUDA graph 不可用 — 在 8× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 上运行 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 并加 --enforce-eager 时解码吞吐极低；请求优先修复 graph 捕获。#56892（另见可用配置的现场报告：#56700）
  2. GDN 解码退化为单个重复 token — Qwen3-Next 在 ROCm（gfx906/MI50）上使用 fp32 SSM cache，上下文增长后出现；在 GB10（sm_121）上启用 prefix caching 时也报告为 CUBLAS 内部错误 / 非法内存访问。#54308、#54173
  3. v0.33.0 回归：b12x attention 非法内存访问 在第一个 MTP verify 步骤（冷 JIT PagedForwardKernel），SM120 + NVFP4 MoE + fp8 KV + chunked prefill + prefix caching；在 v0.32.0 中正常。#65139
  4. 多模态编码器 CUDA graph 崩溃，当 enable_mm_embeds=True + cudagraph_mm_encoder=True 并使用预计算 embeddings 时 — 修复 PR 已开放。#65531、#65535
  5. 编译后的多模块 MTP drafter 在 checkpoint 包含多个 MTP 模块时总是运行模块 0（Qwen3.5/Nex 修复扩展到其余 drafter）— 修复 PR 已开放。#66428
  6. --shutdown-timeout 在 --api-server-count > 1 时从不排空 — API server 在引擎之前停止，进行中的请求以 EngineDeadError（HTTP 500）失败；修复 PR 已开放。#61562
  7. KV pool 饱和时的准入重试使解码 TPOT 膨胀约 2.3 倍（V1 调度器，Ascend P/D 部署）— 请求自动准入退避。#64460
  8. UVA --cpu-offload-gb 在 XPU 上不降低压缩张量 WNA16 MoE 的峰值设备内存。#57008
  9. Anthropic Messages API：不支持 x-api-key 请求头 — 仅 Authorization: Bearer 可用。#51572
  10. Whisper 长音频时间戳漂移（音频 >30s 时每段约 0.5s）— 已关闭。#32588

6. 对应用开发者的意义

  • 有意识地固定你的 vLLM 版本。 v0.33.0 在 SM120 上配合 MTP + prefix caching 存在真实的解码回归（#65139），并将 llguidance 作为无条件依赖发布，在较旧 glibc 上会破坏导入（#66345）。如果你使用消费级 Blackwell 或 RHEL/较旧基础镜像，升级前请先验证。
  • Kimi K3.1 和 MiniMax M3 正成为一等公民。 如果你服务这些系列，请关注 K3.1 TP8 系列和 MiniMax attention 复制标志——后者是跨节点 TP 部署中 attention all-reduce 主导延迟时的务实杠杆。
  • AMD 用户很快将获得有意义的收益 — persistent_topk 采样、调优的 gfx942 FP8 MoE 配置（吞吐 +12–25%）以及提议的 3-bit KV cache 可能大幅降低长上下文工作负载的每 token 成本。
  • 流式/ASR 应用应跟踪调度器持有的持久状态 PR（#65544）；它解锁了无法从 prompt 重新计算会话状态的有状态流式模型——对实时转录和语音代理相关。
  • 运维卫生： --shutdown-timeout 多 API server bug 意味着当前在 DP > 1 部署中优雅排空会静默失败；在 #61562 落地之前，滚动重启期间预期会出现 500。
SGLang — sgl-project/sglang

SGLang 摘要 — 2026-11-09

1. 今日要点

过去 24 小时内没有新的版本发布，但 issue 跟踪器相当繁忙：MoE 模型中报告了一组量化路由器加载 bug（compressed-tensors、FP8），服务器会静默输出垃圾结果而非报错；同时针对 Qwen3.8-NVFP4 提交了一个 prefill CUDA graph logprob 偏差 bug。在性能方面，统一内存 / HiCache 重构 PR 栈正在积极评审中，Rust 服务器后续跟踪器已开启，Q4 Prefill-Decode 分离路线图仍在推进。与此同时，针对 #48399 中 DSV4.1 DeepGEMM indexer 门控变更，报告了 GB10（SM120/121）上 8 倍的 prefill 性能回退。

2. 版本发布与破坏性变更

过去 24 小时无新版本。仍在评审中的重要行为变更项：

  • Qwen4-Exp 的 --boundary-reduction 默认值变更 — PR #49203 提议在 DP attention 下默认使用 reduce-scatter 而非 ar，改变 Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration 和 Qwen4ExpForCausalLMMTP 的解析路径。这会改变现有 Qwen4-Exp 部署的 FFN 出口行为（PR #49203）。
  • 配置结构重构待定：max_running_requests（4096）和 cuda_graph_max_bs（32）的默认值独立推导，超过 graph 上限被描述为吸收态 — 已作为不活跃关闭，但值得在调优指南中注意（Issue #33483）。

3. 新模型与硬件支持

  • SM12x（RTX 50xx / RTX PRO Blackwell）：功能请求将 FlashInfer cuTile NVFP4 MoE 设为 SM12x 上的默认 MoE runner（Issue #49123）。
  • AMD gfx1250 / UALink：carv2 自定义 all-reduce 扩展至 gfx1250 UALink 节点（PR #49003）。
  • AMD AITER FlyDSL causal conv1d prefill 用于 gfx950 上 Qwen3.5/Qwen3.8 GDN 层（可选启用，相较 Triton 路径约 1.1 倍加速）（PR #41879）。
  • AITER 升级就绪跟踪器仍在开放中，逐版本跟踪功能依赖（Issue #21302）。
  • Diffusion / NPU：HiDream-O1-Image 支持（DEV、DEV-2604、FULL TI2I）进行中（PR #45137）。

4. 性能与优化

  • GB10 / SM120–121 DSV4.1 prefill 回退（8 倍）：#48399 将 is_sm100_or_newer() 替换为严格的 current_arch().is_sm(10)，将 SM120/121 从 DeepGEMM indexer 门控中移除，强制回退到 torch 路径并逐层调用 tolist()（Issue #49173）。
  • SM120 上 DeepSeek-V4 dsv4 prefill 仍表现不佳：在相同的 4× RTX PRO 6000 硬件上约 2–7K tok/s，而通过 vLLM/marlin 报告约 12.5K — 请求调优指导（Issue #33422）。
  • FA3 kernel 选择：sglang-kernel FA3 在 H200 上对 hdim 128 非 causal 选择 MmaPV_is_RS=false，比 flash-attn 的 Hopper 构建慢 1.5–3%（Issue #47734）。
  • Prefill 批次 KV 共享：提议在同一 prefill 批次中准入的请求间共享 prompt 的 KV，避免相同 prompt 的冗余全量 prefill 计算（Issue #48963）。
  • 统一内存重构 PR 栈（6 个 PR，#48009–#48014）：按窗口的 host 池/PD 条目、单一布局搜索准入、Triton attention 后端中的多窗口子池支持 — 面向 --enable-unified-memory 和 HiCache 路径（PR #48014、PR #48012）。
  • Rust 服务器栈后续项跟踪非阻塞性能事项（Issue #49055）。
  • 统一 FP32 激活 kernel 位于 sgl_kernel/activation.cuh，带 kFastMath 开关和用于融合量化的 silu_fast（PR #48942）。

5. 稳定性与回退

按严重程度排序：

  1. 量化 MoE 路由器的静默正确性失败 — 严重程度最高。以量化形式（compressed-tensors）存储的路由器从未被加载，服务器返回垃圾结果而不报错（Issue #49185）；Mixtral、Llama 4 和 FP8 Qwen3-MoE 中 FP8 存储的路由器存在相同模式，scale 被丢弃（Issue #49198）。
  2. GLM-5.3-Flash 引擎在一次 1M token 请求后损坏（v0.5.23，MTP 接受率 0.00，所有后续请求退化）；v0.5.22 正常（Issue #48964）。在 GLM-5.3-Flash bug 跟踪器中跟踪（Issue #37524）。
  3. Prefill CUDA graph 数值偏差：短 prefill 填充到捕获桶后产生与 eager 执行不同的 logprob（Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4、混合 GDN、v0.5.23）（Issue #49133）。
  4. 完整 prefill CUDA graph 捕获崩溃 用于混合线性注意力模型（GDN/KDA）— HybridLinearAttnBackend._replay_metadata 中 IndexError（Issue #48593）。
  5. GB10 统一内存在 >40k token prefill 时耗尽 — worker rank 被静默杀死，无 traceback 或 OOM 记录；跨栈控制在 54k 时通过（Issue #36941）。
  6. LoRA use_rslora=True 以错误 scale 服务（Issue #40835）。
  7. 已关闭 / 不活跃：DeepSeek-V4 BF16 checkpoint 被路由到 MXFP4 expert 路径（Issue #44810）；HiCache host 层回载损坏 GLM-5.3-Flash 生成（Issue #38031）；GLM-V 多余多模态占位符导致 500（Issue #37579）。

CI 卫生 PR 正在进行：scheduler stub 在 #49144 后需要 PauseState（PR #49178，已关闭）。来自 hnyls2002 的若干 CI flake 修复已开放 — Mooncake KV 注册启动失败（PR #49156）、Gemma4 AR 融合测试死锁（PR #49160）、以及 diffusion Hub-API 429 回退到缓存快照（PR #49155）。

6. 对应用开发者的意义

  • 在信任输出前审计任何量化 MoE 部署。 路由器加载 bug（#49185、#49198）会静默失败 — 没有报错，只是生成质量差。如果你运行 Mixtral、Llama 4、Qwen3-MoE 或 compressed-tensors/FP8 checkpoint，升级前请对照已知良好参考验证 logits。
  • 将 GLM-5.3-Flash 固定到 v0.5.22，如果你服务长上下文或 1M token 请求；v0.5.23 存在可复现的引擎状态损坏路径（#48964）。
  • 对混合线性注意力 / GDN/KDA 模型以及需要比特精确 logprob 一致性的 NVFP4 checkpoint，禁用或验证完整 prefill CUDA graph（#48593、#49133）。
  • GB10 / DGX Spark 用户：将 prefill 长度限制在 ~40k token 以下，或手动监控 host/统一内存 — OOM 路径会杀死 rank 且无诊断信息（#36941），而 DSV4.1 indexer 回退（#49173）意味着 SM120 上 dsv4 prefill 目前比应有速度慢 8 倍。
  • Agent harness 构建者：关注关于保持多轮 agent 前缀可缓存的 RFC #47763，以及关于同批次前缀 KV 共享的 #48963 — 两者都直接针对 agent 循环的 TTFT 和冗余 prefill 成本（Issue #47763）。
llama.cpp — ggml-org/llama.cpp

llama.cpp 摘要 — 2026-11-09

1. 今日亮点

今天主要是围绕正确性中立的基础设施工作：CUDA/Metal 的 radix Top-K 内核在并列选择时已实现确定性（消除了采样不可复现的一个隐蔽来源），mtmd 多模态栈完成了整合（移除了 clip.h）。性能方面，针对 d_state=64 SSM 扫描的 CUDA 快速路径已落地（为 Zamba2 类架构解锁了此前回退到 CPU 的 GPU 端循环扫描），moe-cache 路径获得了两项重要修复：不再因缓存专家而阻塞 CPU，且投机解码不再将 MoE 缓存应用于草稿模型。开放 issue 队列仍以投机解码（draft-mtp）的正确性/中止报告以及 Intel 硬件上的 Vulkan/SYCL 后端损坏为主。

2. 发布与破坏性变更

无破坏性 API 变更。本窗口内值得注意的构建/行为变更：

  • b12211 — mtmd 重构：移除 clip.h；clip 代码整合进 mtmd。直接包含 clip.h 的第三方消费者（树外 mmproj 工具）必须迁移。（PR #31865）
  • b12208 — 确定性 radix Top-K：CUDA/Metal 的 TOP_K 现在按列顺序解决并列（block → warp → step → lane；最早者胜出）。使用 top_k 的采样输出可能与旧构建略有不同（但稳定）。（PR #31084）
  • b12202 — 精度对齐：ggml_prec_set_acc 调用现在遵循参考实现的精度；GLM4 的 down/output 投影在参考实现不保留 F32 的地方改为 GGML_PREC_BF16。GLM4 系列模型预计会有轻微数值偏移。（PR #31851）
  • b12199 — PEG 工具调用清洗：PEG 工具调用参数中的无效 UTF-8 现已在 common 中清洗；下游解析器不再收到格式错误的字节序列。（PR #31861）

3. 新模型与硬件支持

  • CUDA SSM 扫描 d_state=64 快速路径（b12207）：为 SSM_SCAN 内核中状态大小为 64 的情况补上了缺失的快速路径。Zamba2 风格的循环架构此前每个扫描步都会回退到 CPU；现在在 GPU 上处理。（PR #31818）
  • SpacemiT IME2 MXFP4 稠密重打包（b12210）：面向 RISC-V SpacemiT IME2 加速器的 CPU 端 MXFP4 重打包。（PR #31776）
  • llamafile bf16 + q8_0 VXE（b12209）：llamafile 运行时中针对 bf16 和 q8_0 的新向量扩展路径。（PR #31866）
  • OpenCL q8_0 GEMV + 小 n MoE 验证：新增 kernel_gemv_noshuffle_q8_0_f32_mc 和小 n MoE GEMV 路径，改善 OpenCL 上的投机解码验证（Qualcomm 联合贡献）。（PR #31831）

进行中：

  • PR #31802 — 在 CUDA fattn-mma-f16 内核内融合 q8_0/q4_0 KV 反量化（消除量化 KV 缓存的 f16 暂存物化过程）。
  • PR #30606 — SYCL：将 Battlemage（BMG）D=256 单查询解码路由到 FA 向量内核；报告在 Arc Pro B70、kv=65536、GQA4 下每次调用 832 µs 对比 1150 µs。
  • PR #31896 — MUL_MAT src1 精度测试，以及针对 BF16/F32 精度请求的后端回退到 CPU 的门控（Metal 已拒绝不支持的情况）。

4. 性能与优化

  • MoE 缓存 CPU 解耦（b12206）：CPU 部分不再阻塞等待缓存专家，减少 CPU+GPU 混合 MoE 推理的每 token 停顿。（PR #31888）
  • SSM 扫描 GPU 卸载（b12207）：见上文；消除了 d_state=64 模型的 CPU 回退，这曾是这些架构生成时的主要瓶颈。（PR #31818）
  • CUDA/Metal Top-K 确定性（b12208）：并非提速，但移除了此前的“shift-skip”逻辑和线程时序依赖，使内核行为在多次运行间可复现。（PR #31084）
  • RPC 加载时间改进（开放，PR #29413）：在 2× DGX Spark 上通过 RDMA 加载 DeepSeek-V4-Flash（145.6 GiB）时，load_tensors 快约 5×。
  • IQ2 量化创建提速（开放，PR #31910）：为 IQ2 创建引入模式缓存；作者报告在 8 个模型 / 5 种架构上各 IQ2 类型输出字节一致。
  • 持久化磁盘提示缓存（开放，PR #28092）：--cache-disk 支持混合/SWA 检查点、重启存活、损坏清理和 LRU 磁盘上限驱逐。

5. 稳定性与回归

按严重程度排序：

  1. qwen4exp 上的 draft-mtp kpool 断言 — 服务器在加载时于 llm_graph_input_kpool::set_input 中以 GGML_ASSERT(buffer) 中止。持续被重新报告（#30860、#31914）；#30860 中有提议的修复，据报告可干净地应用到 master。
  2. 量化目标上的投机解码输出偏差（#25618）— 在贪心采样下，当目标模型为量化时，draft-MTP/draft-dspark 输出与非投机运行产生偏差（bf16 下一致）。39 条评论；开放且未解决 — 若你依赖可复现性则相关。
  3. 嵌入请求泄漏 / 服务器静默挂起（#31704）— 被取消的长嵌入永不会被释放；随后服务器不再提供服务，而 /health 仍报告 OK。无修复 PR。
  4. Intel Arc B 系列在长上下文/RAG 下的 Vulkan 损坏（#31828）— 尽管设置了 GGML_VK_DISABLE_COOPMAT 仍存在；开放。
  5. RX 7900 XTX 上 131k 上下文的 Vulkan 78% 解码断崖（#27734，已关闭/失效）— 子分配碎片化；变通方案 GGML_VK_SUBALLOCATION_BLOCK_SIZE=4 GiB。
  6. SYCL AOT 对 >4 GB 模型输出乱码（#31685）— GGML_SYCL_DEVICE_ARCH=arl-h 构建输出 GGGG…；通过缓冲区大小标志缓解。
  7. 循环状态中的粘性 NaN（修复 PR 开放，#31913）— 重置逻辑乘以 0 而非写入 0，使单个 NaN 永久持续；在 RPC 上以 q8 KV 缓存命中 Qwen3.8-flash-next。
  8. 流式响应尽管有 Keep-Alive 仍关闭 TCP 连接（#29680、#31863，已关闭）— 破坏池化 HTTP 客户端。若你对 llama-server 使用 keep-alive 池，请针对你的构建验证。
  9. MoltenVK 着色器越界写入（修复 PR 开放，#31890）— macOS Vulkan 上 test-backend-ops 中的哨兵不匹配。
  10. SYCL -sm tensor 疑似泄漏（#27845，已关闭/失效）— 双 Intel B70，报告于生成期间。

6. 对应用开发者的意义

  • 投机解码仍是最有风险的旋钮。 若你依赖确定性输出（评估框架、回归测试、agent 回放），要么使用 bf16 目标，要么在量化目标上禁用 draft-MTP/dspark，要么固定一个已知良好的构建。今日两大 issue 中有两个是投机解码正确性/中止 bug。
  • 工具调用鲁棒性悄然改善。 UTF-8 清洗（b12199）以及开放的语法排序 PR（#30193，Qwen3-Coder/Nemotron 参数键排序）和 Gemma4 宽松 schema 语法工作（#31915）都针对最常见的 agent 失败模式：格式错误的工具参数。若你在 Qwen/Nemotron/Gemma 上运行 agent，请跟踪这些。
  • 健康检查并不充分。 Issue #31704（嵌入槽泄漏而 /health 健康）提醒你要监控实际吞吐/延迟，而不仅是存活。开放的 UI 性能视图（#31893）若合并，将在 llama-ui 中展示 /metrics 数据。
  • 混合 CPU/GPU MoE 服务变得更好。 b12206 消除了 moe-cache 中的同步停顿；结合 --moe-cache-cpu-share auto 工作（#31286），部分卸载的 MoE 部署应能看到更平稳的 token 节奏。
  • 持久化提示缓存即将到来。 --cache-disk（#28092）将为重放长系统提示的 RAG/agent 工作负载显著降低冷启动延迟 — 若你频繁重启服务器，值得原型验证。
  • 树外 mmproj 集成者：现在就处理 mtmd 重构。 自 b12211 起 clip.h 已移除；任何包含它的代码在升级时都会中断。
Ollama — ollama/ollama

Ollama 摘要 — 2026-11-09

1. 今日亮点

过去 24 小时内没有新版本发布，但 PR 队列活跃，主要集中在后端与调度器的正确性工作上：Rockchip NPU 支持（#19480）、无损 FP8 导入并保持一致的 MoE 专家堆叠（#19614），以及一个调度器修复，使无法停止的 runner 保留在已加载集合中以防止 VRAM 超额分配（#19581）。在 Issue 跟踪器中，780M 上的 AMD Vulkan 回归（#17748）和企业代理环境下 ollama pull 返回 403（#19604）仍然处于开放状态，而长期被请求的按模型 num_parallel 功能现已在 PR #9546 中实现。

2. 版本发布与破坏性变更

无。过去 24 小时内没有新版本；没有 API/配置变更落地。

3. 新模型与硬件支持

  • Rockchip NPU 后端（RK3588/RK3576） — PR #19480 新增了 rocket/rknpu 后端，将提示处理（MUL_MAT、MUL_MAT_ID、FLASH_ATTN_EXT）卸载到 NPU，同时将单 token 解码保留在 CPU 上。PR #19480
  • 无损 FP8 导入 + 一致的 MoE 专家堆叠 — PR #19614 统一了所有源类型的专家堆叠方式（修复了此前以未堆叠专家形式发布的 MoE 模型），并新增了逐张量 FP8 导入；块 FP8 不再被有损地重新量化为 mxfp8。PR #19614
  • Docker 中的 Nvidia MLX/Vulkan — PR #18592 补充了缺失的库/配置，使 MLX runner 和 Vulkan 驱动在容器内配合 Nvidia GPU 正常工作。PR #18592
  • 图像生成模型 — 目前在 macOS 上不受支持：ollama run x/flux2-klein 会报错“image generation models are not currently supported”（#19615，已关闭）。尚不是受支持的路径。Issue #19615
  • 第三方架构请求 — 有人提交了对“OSADIA Axiom”架构支持的请求（#19611）；没有迹象表明会被接受。Issue #19611

4. 性能与优化

  • 混合模型与量化 KV 缓存的精确 VRAM 预测 — PR #19609 修复了 PredictServerVRAM，该方法此前对每个块都假定全上下文注意力 KV（对循环 SSM 块 / full_attention_interval 而言是错误的），并且始终将 KV 按未量化的 f16 计费。这直接影响 GPU/CPU 放置决策。PR #19609
  • Metal 预填充分块收缩 — PR #19280 随着上下文增长而减小预填充分块大小，防止 macOS GPU 看门狗在超长提示（例如大型 XML 文件）下杀死进程。PR #19280
  • 按模型并行度 — PR #9546 新增了可通过环境变量和 Modelfile 控制的 num_parallel，因此小模型（例如嵌入模型）的上下文不再被服务器级的 OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL 三倍放大。解决了 #8842 以及已关闭的 #11977/#5693。PR #9546
  • 上下文缓冲区填充生成 — PR #9547 允许 num_predict==-2 生成直到上下文缓冲区填满，与 llama.cpp 语义一致。PR #9547
  • 基准测试工具可靠性 — PR #19600 使 cmd/bench 在运行不完整时以非零状态退出，并截断复用的输出文件。PR #19600

5. 稳定性与回归

按严重程度排序：

  1. AMD Radeon 780M Vulkan 回归（开放，无修复 PR） — Ollama ≥0.32.10 在较大模型上失败，报 radv/amdgpu: Not enough memory for command submission / ErrorDeviceLost；相同硬件在旧版本上正常。Issue #17748
  2. 卸载失败时的调度器 VRAM 超额分配（修复 PR 已开放） — 当杀死 runner 失败时，调度器仍会释放模型，按满 GPU 进行预测，倾向 CPU，并可能启动第二个 llama-server。PR #19581 将无法停止的 runner 保留在已加载集合中。Issue #19577 / PR #19581
  3. 企业代理后 ollama pull 返回 403（开放） — Blue Coat / RHEL 9.2 环境中 curl 正常但 systemd 服务返回 403；4 条评论，尚未解决。Issue #19604
  4. 更新后资源回归报告（开放） — 用户报告在 15.4G RAM / 8G RTX 5060 Laptop 配置上运行 ministral-3 14B，版本更新后行为变差：资源占用更高且输出“更僵硬”。需要分诊。Issue #19537
  5. Gemma4 工具调用解析器 bug（修复 PR 已开放） — 45 个标量字符串后跟一个双字符串数组时，可能因占位符冲突（NUL,comma,NUL）而静默丢弃一个有效的工具调用。PR #18355
  6. Gemma4 QAT 元数据拼写错误（已关闭） — gemma4:12b-it-qat 的 Modelfile 键为 toos 而非 tools，破坏了该模型的工具支持。Issue #19596
  7. GGUF 解析加固（PR 已开放） — 拒绝重复张量名（#19571）、零维张量（#19607）和非 2 的幂对齐（#19610）；此前这些能通过元数据解析，仅在加载/检查时失败。PR #19571 · PR #19607 · PR #19610
  8. CLI 噪音 — ollama -v/--version 会输出“could not connect to a running Ollama instance”警告；输出整洁性回归。Issue #19613
  9. 上下文截断丢弃最后一条用户消息 — chatPrompt() 按类型无关的位置保留最后一条消息，因此尾部的工具调用消息可能挤掉实际的最终用户轮次。PR #19058

较低优先级：快速写入时 WriteWithBackup 时间戳冲突（#19608）、应用中吞掉服务器启动错误（#19179），以及未设置 API 字段导致的模型抖动（#10003）。

6. 对应用开发者的意义

  • 多模型部署获得更精细的控制。 一旦 #9546 落地，你可以按模型调整 num_parallel，而不必全局承担上下文倍数税——如果你将嵌入模型与聊天模型共同托管，这一点很重要。
  • 如果你使用 AMD Vulkan，请为已知回归做好准备。 780M iGPU 用户请固定使用 0.32.10 以下的版本，或在升级前跟踪 #17748。
  • 企业/代理环境： TLS 检查代理后 ollama pull 失败（#19604）仍然开放；请验证 systemd 服务的代理 CA 处理，而不仅仅是你的 shell。
  • Gemma4 上的 Agent 工具调用： 关注 #18355（解析器冲突静默丢弃工具调用）和 #19596（已修复的 toos 元数据拼写错误）；如果你依赖工具，请重新拉取 QAT 模型。
  • VRAM 规划很快会改善。 混合/量化 KV 的 VRAM 预测修复（#19609）将使 SSM 混合模型和量化缓存模型的 GPU 卸载决策更准确——合并后预期 CPU 倾向的意外会减少。
  • 边缘部署扩展： Rockchip NPU 后端（#19480）值得在预填充成为瓶颈的 RK3588/RK3576 板卡上评估。
LiteLLM — BerriAI/litellm

LiteLLM 摘要 — 2026-11-09

    • Open Uncensored（Chat Completions + 原生 Responses 路由）— https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/50564

  • SpendLogDelivery 核算指标（已关闭）：AccountingDeliveryRepository.metrics() 在每次 flush 时扫描所有保留的 LiteLLM_SpendLogDelivery 行；问题已关闭，暗示采用了有界查询修复。https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/50475
  • JSON 日志密钥扫描（开放）：在 JSON 日志格式化期间对未变更字符串进行冗余的正则/密钥扫描；与早前的病态正则问题 #32353 不同。https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/40247
  • 递归工具 schema（开放，已停滞）：unpack_defs 在 $defs/$ref 高扇入 schema 上仍然无界；Bedrock 和 Vertex 调用方不传递字节预算。在对抗性或生成的工具 schema 上存在数秒至挂起的风险。https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/34328

5. 稳定性与回归（按严重程度排序）

高 — 计费/正确性

  • 用量缺失/格式异常时密钥预算未扣费 — 当 OpenAI 兼容上游省略 usage 时，支出永不记录，max_budget 永不关闭；在按 9 次规模设置的预算上，20/20 次调用成功（上游计费 +100.5%）。格式异常的 usage（{"prompt_tokens":"oops",...}）表现出相同故障。https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/50124
  • /v1/responses 断连遗留完整 Redis 预算预留 — 在首 token 前取消的流式请求记录 HTTP 499，但保留 finalized=false 的预留不变。https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/50528
  • max_budget 允许超预算调用 — 在适合 9 次的预算上，即使串行也有 11 次调用被允许（不仅仅是突发竞态）。https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/50125
  • Anthropic 服务端回退定价错误 — 每次回退尝试都按应答模型的费率定价，且未计费的拒绝被计入。修复 PR 开放中（标记为破坏性）。https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/50556

高 — 协议/转换

  • /v1/messages 返回误导性 503 — 任何非 ProxyException 的上游故障（例如连接被拒绝）都表现为 "authentication database is temporarily unreachable"，误导运维人员；/v1/chat/completions 返回正确的 50x。https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/49998
  • 无法解析的 200 被抛出为 500 — 提供商返回 HTTP 200 但非 JSON 或 JSON 缺少 choices；litellm 抛出晦涩的 APIError 并丢弃 usage，导致调用方重试一个已计费的请求。https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/49793
  • Bedrock Invoke /v1/messages 流在分离排空中止后未关闭 — 当 ANTHROPIC_MESSAGES_MAX_DETACHED_STREAM_DRAINS=0 时，客户端断连后上游继续生成；httpx 响应永不关闭。https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/50514
  • Claude 上的 reasoning_effort="none" — 剥离 thinking 配置而非显式禁用，导致上游默认开启的 thinking 保持活跃（已关闭）。https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/47924
  • Amazon Nova 流式 100% 失败 — httpx zstd 解码器在 Nova 多帧 SSE 间复用已完成的 decompressobj（已关闭）。https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/35589
  • /v1/messages 上部署级 extra_body 被丢弃 — 按部署配置的 Anthropic 服务端回退被静默忽略；修复 PR 开放于 PR #50558 及路由器合并变体 PR #49839（标记为破坏性）。https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/50558
  • /v1/audio/speech Qwen3-TTS — 强制 voice 参数和自定义参数被剥离（开放）。https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/20078

中 — 路由/可观测性

  • Arize Phoenix 重复计数 — 代理父 span litellm_proxy_request 重复 LLM 属性，因此 Phoenix 在旧路径（未设置 LITELLM_OTEL_V2）上对每次调用定价两次。修复 PR 开放中。https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/50649 / https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/50655
  • 路由器重试忽略调用方超时 — x-litellm-timeout 仅约束每次尝试；Retry-After 休眠不检查调用方剩余预算。https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/49751
  • MCP 访问组列表泄露范围 — GET /v1/mcp/access_groups 返回密钥无法查看/调用的服务器上的组；修复 PR 开放中。https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/50650
  • MCP 每请求认证头被忽略 — 当未配置静态凭据时，x-mcp-{alias}-authorization 解析为无认证。https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/35403
  • trim_messages 在带前缀模型上无操作 — openai/gpt-4o、anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 完全跳过裁剪；在多模态列表内容和 None 内容上也会失败。修复 PR 开放中。https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/50639 / https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/50645 / https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/50648
  • OpenAI Agents SDK + Bedrock 上的 Claude — 工具搜索后找不到延迟工具，搜索记录在后续轮次丢失，压缩参数在 /v1/messages 上被丢弃。https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/50104

低

  • utils.py 中的 ModelNotMappedError 报告无复现数据。https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/47922
  • user_url_allowed_hosts 在 litellm_settings 下被忽略（已关闭）。https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/35177
  • 编辑 MCP stdio 服务器会擦除存储的环境变量。https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/28903
  • UI 回调覆盖配置定义的回调（已关闭）。https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/12118

6. 对应用开发者的意义

  • 目前不要将 max_budget 视为硬性支出上限。 三个独立问题（#50124、#50125、#50528）表明，当用量缺失、并发高或流被取消时，预算会超额服务。如果你要强制执行成本上限，请在上游侧添加防护（提供商预算/配额），而不是仅信任网关。
  • 重试逻辑需要感知“无法解析的 200”情况。 问题 #49793 意味着你的 SDK 可能对一次成功计费的上游调用看到 500 形态的错误；盲目重试 acompletion 可能导致双重计费。考虑使用幂等键或在重试前按 request_id 去重。
  • Anthropic /v1/messages 消费者应谨慎固定版本。 多个进行中的修复被标记为破坏性（fix(responses)!、fix(router)!）并触及 extra_body 合并语义。如果你依赖按部署的 extra_body 实现 Anthropic 服务端回退，它目前在 /v1/messages 上不会到达线上——升级越过 PR #50558 / #49839 后请测试。
  • 面向调用方的超时不是总预算边界。 根据问题 #49751，x-litellm-timeout 约束每次尝试；一连串 Retry-After 重试可能超出你预期的挂钟时间。请在客户端强制执行总截止时间。
  • 可观测性成本重复计数： 如果你通过旧回调路径使用 Arize Phoenix，在 PR #50655 落地前预计会有约 2 倍的成本归属。或者设置 LITELLM_OTEL_V2。
  • 工具 schema 卫生很重要 — 具有高扇入的递归 $defs/$ref schema 可能在 Bedrock/Vertex 上触发无界的 unpack_defs 路径；请在 agent 工具定义中预展平或约束生成的 schema。
Unsloth — unslothai/unsloth

Unsloth 摘要 — 2026-11-09

今日亮点

过去 24 小时内没有新版本发布，但 PR 队列非常活跃：一大批由 danielhanchen 编写的 Studio/扩散修复被合并（许多在当天即 CLOSED），此外还有针对 Turing INT8 支持和并发模型加载线程安全修复的开放后续 PR。今天的主线是 Studio 的图像/视频扩散路径（fp8 降噪器、NVFP4、INT8 内核、VAE 解码回退）以及围绕“设置→外观”的 UI 打磨。两个开放的功能请求（#16980、#17126）表明，对 Studio 中检查点保留和图像编辑端点的需求正在增长。

发布与破坏性变更

过去 24 小时内无。未公布 API/配置变更。

新模型与硬件支持

  • [OPEN] Studio：T4/Turing 上的 INT8（sm75） — 解除 dense_transformer_supported 拒绝，使 transformer_quant="int8" 能在 Turing GPU 上运行，而不是在加载前报错。#17167
  • [OPEN] 仅支持 fp16 的 GPU 上的 FLUX.3 — 按存储保留 bf16 权重，并逐层以 float32 计算，避免 #17124 引入的完整 float32 主机内存物化。#17173
  • [CLOSED] 编译版 ROCm W8A8 线性的按卡判定 — 此前按进程缓存；现在按卡判定，因此 RDNA3→RDNA4（或反之）的序列能选中正确的内核。#17078
  • [OPEN] LLM 训练页面：constant 和 constant_with_warmup 学习率调度器 — 仅 UI 层面暴露后端已接受的调度器。#17168
  • [Bug] Intel Arc 140V（桌面应用） — 图像生成模型无法加载。#17137
  • [Bug] gfx1031（RX 6700 XT）上的 ROCm Docker — 启动检查以“RDNA 2”通过，但 PyTorch 在首次 GPU 操作时段错误。#17147

性能与优化

  • [CLOSED] Qwen-Image-2.1 CFG 配对 — 启用真实 CFG 的块流式渲染此前每一步都会将每个流式块上传两次；现在引导分支按流式块配对。#17111
  • [CLOSED] MiniMax-H3 条件器内存 — 仅保留 H3 实际读取的隐藏状态（hidden_states[50]）；在 50 层 Qwen3-VL 条件器上，4096 token 时节省约 2 GiB。#17095
  • [CLOSED] 加载预取 — 通过 mincore 跳过已在页缓存中的块，并按工作线程预算读缓冲区（此前无条件为 64 MiB × 8 工作线程）。#17112
  • [CLOSED] 图像后处理 — uint8_hwc 现在按行条带转换，每行条带各做一次 float32 拷贝，而不是物化整个批次。#17091
  • [CLOSED] INT8 融合 MLP / v2 Linear — 在 _act_quant_device_ok 已验证与 torchao 位级一致的情况下，输入使用探测的单遍 Triton 内核量化。#17114
  • [CLOSED] 排队的图像生成 — 现在等待各自的池，而不是占用默认执行器的工作线程。#17108
  • [OPEN] 扩散 Triton 内核的设备定向 — diffusion_vae_fused.py 中的九处启动此前隐式地在当前线程的 CUDA 设备上启动；PR #17099（CLOSED）修复为使用输入张量所在的卡。
  • [CLOSED] NVFP4 保护分支 — 消除第二次相同调用时的重新编译（冷解码表记忆），并接受 fp16 输入。#17081

稳定性与回归

按严重程度排序：

  1. 高 — L4（sm_89）上的 fp8 降噪器挂起：FLUX.3 klein fp8 在 torch < 2.12 下于 captured Flux3Transformer2DModel graph 1/4 处无限挂起。修复 PR 已开放：#17166。
  2. 高 — 并发扩散加载线程不安全：init_empty_weights 全局修补 torch；并发骨架构建可能使 torch 保持被修补状态，导致间歇性 399 tensor(s) ... 加载失败。修复 PR 已开放：#17171。
  3. 中 — CPU 后端上 MoE 路由器辅助损失发散：在 UNSLOTH_FORCE_CPU=1 下，流水线并行 + 梯度累积 > 1 训练出的损失与单进程不同；仓库自带的奇偶校验测试可复现。尚无修复 PR。#17054
  4. 中 — 托管账户忽略已保存的 HF token：尽管 token 有效，门控模型（如 FLUX.1-dev）仍被拒绝。修复 PR 已开放：#17172。
  5. 中 — 视频 VAE 解码回退仅匹配 Windows 分配器错误：未识别 Linux/macOS 的分配器拒绝拼写。已修复（CLOSED）：#17075。
  6. 低 — LoRA fuse 主机备份可能钉住集成 GPU 内存 / 超出主机 RAM 预留。已修复（CLOSED）：#17086。
  7. 低 — Studio 设置 UI：调色板及其他外观选择器在每次选择后关闭。修复 PR 已开放：#17164、#17170；重复的玻璃材质控件 #17162，撰写器设置分散在多个标签页 #17163。
  8. 低 — 模型大小不匹配：Model Hub 与 Model Picker 下拉菜单之间不一致。#17074

对应用开发者的意义

  • 扩散工作负载是当前活跃的前沿。 许多当天 CLOSED 的 PR 针对图像/视频渲染（CFG 配对、NVFP4、INT8、VAE 分块、设备定向）。如果你用 Studio 做图像/视频生成，请固定到已知良好的提交——若干修复刚落地，且 fp8/Turing 路径仍有未解决的回归。
  • Turing（T4）用户在开放 PR 中获得 INT8 和安全的 FLUX.3 fp16 渲染——如果你在较旧的云端 GPU 上提供服务，这与你相关。
  • 并发加载尚不安全。 如果你的部署会并发（或按请求）加载多个扩散模型，请在启用该模式前关注 #17171。
  • 托管/组织部署：门控仓库需要 #17172 中的修复；在合并之前，托管账户无法使用自己的 HF token。
  • MoE + CPU 训练（流水线并行、梯度累积 > 1）目前不正确——不要依赖它来保证损失奇偶一致性。
  • 值得跟踪的功能请求：图像 LoRA 运行期间的检查点保留（#16980）和图像编辑端点（通过外部 OpenAI 兼容服务器的 /v1/images/edits，#17126）——两者都会影响 Studio 自动化流水线。

本日报由 agents-radar 自动生成。

item.content:encoded:
AI Infrastructure Digest 2026-11-09

Generated: 2026-11-08 23:13 UTC | Projects covered: 6

  • vLLM
  • SGLang
  • llama.cpp
  • Ollama
  • LiteLLM
  • Unsloth

Cross-Project Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — 2026-11-09

1. Ecosystem Overview

Today's digests show a mature AI infrastructure stack converging on three fronts simultaneously: Blackwell/SM120 consumer-GPU enablement is still rocky across every serving engine (vLLM and SGLang both have open decode/prefill regressions on RTX PRO 6000 / GB10 hardware), quantized MoE serving has become the dominant correctness surface (SGLang reports two silent-garbage router-loading bugs; vLLM has an SM120+NVFP4+MTP illegal-memory-access regression), and AMD/ROCm is receiving serious investment (vLLM's persistent_topk and gfx942 FP8 MoE configs, SGLang's gfx1250 UALink and AITER FlyDSL paths). Meanwhile the gateway layer is absorbing more production responsibility — LiteLLM's queue shows spend-accounting and protocol-translation bugs mattering as much as routing throughput. Local runtimes (llama.cpp, Ollama) are converging on the same themes from the other direction: speculative-decoding correctness, MoE partial offload, and hardware-diversity backends (RISC-V, Rockchip NPU, SYCL/Vulkan).

2. Activity Comparison

Project Issues (24h) PRs (24h) Release Status Notable Signal
vLLM High (10 ranked regressions + active RFCs) Heavy in-flight (Kimi K3.1 TP8 series, Marlin→Humming) No release in 24h; v0.33.0 carries known SM120 regression Largest structural optimization proposal in flight (Humming kernel migration)
SGLang High (56-ticket-style backlog implied; 10 ranked) Active (unified-memory refactor stack, Rust server follow-ups) No release in 24h; v0.5.23 has GLM-5.3-Flash corruption Highest-severity correctness bugs (silent MoE router failures)
llama.cpp Moderate (10 ranked) Heavy merge day (b12202–b12211 landed; new clip.h removal) ~10 builds landed (b12199–b12211) Most releases of any project; deterministic Top-K is a reproducibility win
Ollama Moderate (9 ranked) Active (Rockchip NPU, FP8 import, VRAM prediction) No release in 24h Per-model num_parallel finally implemented (#9546)
LiteLLM Very high (56 issues updated) Very high (304 PRs touched) Dev tag v1.110.0-dev.2 (cosign-signed images) Highest churn; billing correctness bugs dominate
Unsloth Moderate (bug reports) Very high (large same-day CLOSED batch + open follow-ups) No release in 24h Diffusion/Studio path is the active frontier

Reading the table: LiteLLM's issue/PR volume is an order of magnitude above the serving engines — partly gateway-surface breadth, partly the cost of owning billing semantics. llama.cpp is the only project shipping continuous builds, which is consistent with its role as the low-level reference runtime.

3. Model Support Race

Model / Architecture vLLM SGLang llama.cpp Ollama Unsloth
Kimi K3.1 (TP8) ✅ Split 3/5 in flight — — — —
MiniMax M3 / M3.1 ✅ Attention replication flag + NVFP4 index shard — — — —
Nemotron 3.5 ASR streaming 🟡 FR + persistent-state PR — — — —
Qwen3.5/3.8 (GDN hybrid) 🟡 MTP drafter fix ✅ AITER causal conv1d prefill ✅ SSM d_state=64 fast path — ✅ Qwen-Image CFG fix
DeepSeek-V4.1 — 🟡 8× prefill regression on SM120 ✅ RPC load 5× faster (open) — —
Mixtral / Llama 4 / Qwen3-MoE (FP8 routers) — 🔴 Silent router bug — — —
GLM-5.3-Flash / GLM-V — 🔴 v0.5.23 engine corruption — — —
FLUX.3 / HiDream / image-gen — ✅ HiDream-O1-Image (in progress) — ❌ Unsupported on macOS ✅ fp8/fp16/Turing paths
InternLM3 / TeleChat2/3 ✅ HF Transformers backend migration — — — —
Rockchip RK3588/RK3576 — — — ✅ NPU prefill backend —

Who is ahead: vLLM leads on breadth of new frontier-model support (Kimi, MiniMax, Nemotron) and is standardizing on the HF Transformers backend for long-tail architectures — a strategic bet that reduces per-model maintenance. SGLang is ahead on AMD-specific model paths (AITER for Qwen GDN on gfx950) and diffusion. llama.cpp owns the architecture-generic wins (SSM scan, MXFP4 RISC-V repack). Ollama is the only project pushing to non-GPU accelerators (Rockchip NPU) — a distinct edge-deployment bet.

4. Performance Frontier

Optimization effort is concentrated in four clusters, with uneven distribution:

KV cache — the hottest frontier. vLLM has the most aggressive agenda: a proposed 3-bit Octave KV cache for AMD (#59773), plus caching K/V view derivation in Triton/eager backends. llama.cpp has fused q8_0/q4_0 KV dequant inside CUDA fattn-mma-f16 in progress (#31802) and a sticky-NaN fix for recurrent state (#31913). SGLang is attacking redundant prefill KV via same-batch prefix sharing (#48963). Ollama's contribution is forecasting — accurate hybrid/quantized-KV VRAM prediction (#19609).

Quantization — where correctness risk lives. SGLang's silent MoE router bugs (#49185, #49198) are today's most severe issue precisely because quantized routers fail without error. vLLM's Marlin→Humming migration (#65560) is the largest structural kernel change in flight, consolidating INT4/FP8/MXFP*/NVFP4 paths across NVIDIA architectures. Unsloth's INT8-fused MLP work (#17114) and Turing INT8 enablement (#17167) extend quantized training/inference to older hardware.

Kernels & backends — AMD/Blackwell are the targets. vLLM: ROCm persistent_topk (#63847), gfx942 FP8 MoE (+12–25% throughput, #63727). SGLang: FlyDSL causal conv1d, gfx1250 UALink all-reduce, FA3 kernel-selection tuning (1.5–3% gap). llama.cpp: SYCL Battlemage decode path, OpenCL q8_0 GEMV for speculative verification.

Distributed serving & scheduling. vLLM's MiniMax attention-replication flag is a pragmatic cross-node TP lever; SGLang's unified-memory/HiCache refactor (6 PRs) and Q4 P/D disaggregation roadmap are the most structured effort; Ollama's scheduler VRAM-overcommit fix (#19581) is the local-runtime analogue.

Notable absence: batching-level innovation is sparse today — most gains are kernel- and memory-layout-level, not scheduler-level (SGLang's max_running_requests/cuda_graph_max_bs interaction remains an absorbing-state tuning trap, #33483).

5. Layer Positioning

Layer Project(s) Primary Value Today's Focus
Serving engine (datacenter) vLLM, SGLang Throughput, frontier-model day-one support, distributed serving Kimi/MiniMax support, Blackwell fixes, AMD kernels, silent-correctness bugs
Local/edge runtime llama.cpp, Ollama Portability, hardware diversity, single-binary/desktop UX Deterministic sampling, SSM offload, Rockchip NPU, per-model parallelism
LLM gateway LiteLLM Routing, budgets, protocol translation, observability Spend-accounting correctness, /v1/messages fidelity, hot-path Python elimination
Training / fine-tuning Unsloth Memory-efficient training, diffusion Studio, quantization-aware fine-tuning Diffusion pipeline fixes, INT8/Turing, thread-safe concurrent loads

The layers are converging on overlapping responsibilities: vLLM and SGLang now both implement OpenAI-ish API surfaces and gateway-like routing (P/D disaggregation, fallback); LiteLLM is moving hot paths into Rust to survive 1,000+ deployments; Ollama is absorbing runtime concerns (VRAM prediction, scheduler) that used to be implicit. Expect continued pressure on the gateway layer's traditional role as litellm pushes perf-critical logic into Rust and serving engines expose richer native APIs.

6. Trend Signals

1. Silent correctness failures are the defining risk of quantized MoE. SGLang's router bugs (#49185, #49198) serve garbage with no error; vLLM's SM120/NVFP4/MTP regression (#65139) and llama.cpp's spec-decode divergence on quantized targets (#25618) are the same class. Action for developers: build logit-parity or golden-output tests against a reference checkpoint before any quantized-MoE upgrade — liveness checks won't catch these.

2. Budget enforcement cannot be trusted at the gateway layer alone. LiteLLM's #50124/#50125/#50528 trio (missing usage → uncharged; over-budget admitted serially; disconnect leaves reservations) means max_budget is best-effort. Action: pair gateway budgets with upstream provider quotas and client-side total deadlines (x-litellm-timeout bounds per-attempt, not wall clock, #49751).

3. Speculative decoding is a reproducibility hazard, not just a perf knob. Two top-3 llama.cpp issues are spec-decode correctness/abort (#30860/#31914, #25618). Action: if you run eval harnesses, agent replay, or regression suites, either use bf16 targets or disable draft-MTP on quantized models and pin a build.

4. Blackwell consumer GPUs (SM120) are not production-ready across engines. vLLM decode collapse (#56892) and SGLang's 8× DSV4.1 prefill regression (#49173, from an over-strict is_sm(10) gate) both point to immature SM120 paths. Action: RTX 50xx / RTX PRO 6000 / GB10 deployments should validate against SM100-class reference numbers and track the fixes, not assume feature parity.

5. AMD is becoming a first-class serving target — with model-specific tuning. Octave 3-bit KV, gfx942 FP8 MoE configs, gfx1250 UALink, AITER GDN kernels. Action: if MI300X/MI355 or RDNA is in your roadmap, budget for engine-specific kernel enablement; don't assume CUDA-tuned configs transfer.

6. Streaming/agent infrastructure is the next battleground. vLLM's scheduler-owned persistent state (#65544) unlocks stateful ASR/voice agents; SGLang's cacheable-agent-prefix RFC (#47763) and same-batch KV sharing (#48963) target agent-loop TTFT; llama.cpp's UTF-8 tool-call sanitization (b12199) and grammar-ordering PRs address the most common agent failure mode. Action: agent harness builders should track these three threads — they directly affect TTFT, tool-call reliability, and multi-turn cost.

7. Graceful operations are still under-served. vLLM's --shutdown-timeout bug (#61562) means rolling restarts on DP>1 deployments drop in-flight requests with 500s; Ollama's runner-unload failure can overcommit VRAM (#19577). Action: for production rolling upgrades, validate drain behavior explicitly and expect 500s until the vLLM fix lands.

8. Diffusion/image-gen is the emerging workload class in fine-tuning stacks. Unsloth's same-day CLOSED batch is overwhelmingly diffusion (CFG pairing, NVFP4 decode, VAE tiling, device targeting), with open fp8-on-L4 and thread-safety regressions. Action: if Studio-driven image/video pipelines are in scope, pin commits and avoid concurrent diffusion model loads until #17171 lands.
